label: Late-original / delimiter / first-copy-steps window in long sequences (content-gated)
explanation: Positional window unit. It is active from about step 6 onward, but only up to the third copy output (recall_idx <= 2): the last few original tokens, the <DEL> step (rate 16%, 29% of mass), and the first 1-3 copy steps. It never fires at t <= 2 and almost never in short sequences (L <= 5). Rate and magnitude climb with L (L=9 holds 54% of mass) and peak around t=7-9, with the maximum usually at or right before <DEL>. There is a weak secondary bump at the very end of L=8-9 copies. Inside the window, whether it fires depends on content in a diffuse way. It is more likely when the first original tokens, i.e. the outputs coming up, are x, e, f, r, o or 0, and the top examples almost all start with x or f. No small token set captures this gating (best content-gated F1 about 0.36). The window predicate covers 86% of activation mass, but only about 15% of window steps are active, so precision is poor. It does not fire in the middle or late copy phase of short and medium sequences, or early in the original phase.
